collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A grieving villager does not want a public mourning ceremony: respect it, or hold a small one anyway.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s father has died, and the village is preparing the usual mourning gathering, with songs and food and speeches. (subject) has asked them not to. (subject.He/she) wants to say goodbye alone. (friend), who is organizing it, is worried that the village needs to grieve too. What should (friend) do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) cancels the gathering. (subject) spends the day by the sea, alone. The village grieves quietly, in its own huts. A few days later, (subject) thanks (friend), and tells (friend.him/her) one small story about (subject.his/her) father. (friend) keeps it to (friend.him/her)self.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) holds a small gathering for those who want to remember (subject)'s father, without (subject). (subject) hears the singing from down on the beach. (subject.He/she) does not come, but (subject.he/she) is not angry either. Later, (subject.he/she) asks (friend) which songs they sang.
